claims.text: The baseline system is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The baseline coating has a thin, conventionally formed native oxide layer.
The baseline native oxide is less uniform than the oxide produced by controlled pre-oxidation.
Controlled pre-oxidation will produce a thicker oxide layer on the coating.
Controlled pre-oxidation will produce a more uniform and chemically stable oxide layer.
Thermally activated oxidation and wear mechanisms are significant under the intended high-temperature sliding conditions.
Oxide-layer thickness, uniformity, and chemical composition govern the coating's sliding response.
The deliberately formed oxide layer acts as a thermally stable interfacial barrier.
The oxide barrier minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact reduces adhesive wear.
The deliberately formed oxide layer limits micro-crack initiation and propagation.
Micro-crack initiation and propagation drive microscopic plastic deformation.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have lower wear rates than untreated baseline coatings during high-temperature sliding.
Pre-oxidized coatings will exhibit less microscopic deformation, including less grain-boundary sliding and fewer micro-cracks, than baseline coatings.
The predicted wear and deformation benefits apply only while the oxide layer remains stable during high-temperature sliding.
Temperatures beyond the oxide's stability range or conditions causing rapid oxide degradation may eliminate the predicted benefits.
Concurrent thermal aging and interactions with the substrate may influence wear and deformation outcomes.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes or qualifies conditions in which the oxide degrades, stating that benefits may not hold there, whereas the falsification rule treats oxide degradation with comparable or worse wear as falsifying the hypothesis. A result outside the stated stability regime therefore ambiguously serves both as an exception and as falsification.
